ADR text (for DECISIONS.md): "ADR-0xx Simulation clicks are counted by a beacon, not by the page render. /t and /q only look the token up; the client sends simulationClickAction once on mount and the fake sign-in appears after it. Known scanner user agents and prefetches are refused at the beacon. Trade-off: a JavaScript-less client is not counted; a sandbox that detonates in a real browser still counts, so allow-listing (docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md) remains required. Simulation mail may go out from a look-alike address only after the organisation proves that domain with its TXT record (the same value as Branding → Domain proof); the proof is one-time (no daily re-check), stored in settings.email.simulationDomain, and is used for kind 'simulation' only. Base images are pinned by multi-arch index digest; Node security releases arrive through Dependabot's weekly digest bump."

approve
Reviewed worktree wf_42496c94-3d0-4 at cd4717e (two commits on top of 1a45970: fea9051 plus the review-fix commit cd4717e, which the brief did not list but which is part of the branch). Read-only; nothing edited or committed.

Attacker checks done: (a) bypass of the click guard — the page render never records; the beacon is a server action gated by token regex, via check and isLikelyScanner (headers() works in actions); recordSubmit now needs clickedAt so a forged submit without a click records nothing; drill.ts still calls recordClick then recordSubmit directly and keeps working. Replay/race: recordClick and recordSubmit claim with conditional UPDATE … WHERE … IS NULL, idempotent under concurrency. (b) sender address — z.email + normaliseHost, exact-domain equality against the stored proven domain, decided again inside the row lock in saveEmailAction, verify path shares the 20/h DNS budget, proof record is per-tenant HMAC so no cross-tenant proof or adoption; mail.ts uses simulationAddress only for outbox.kind === "simulation" (test confirms welcome mail keeps the ordinary From). Client cannot inject simulationDomain (not in emailSchema; carried from the locked row). emailView passes the two new fields through via rest spread. (c) docs linked from portal/README.md, docs/API.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. (d) Dockerfile and both compose digests verified live against registry-1.docker.io: both tags return Content-Type application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json with exactly the committed Docker-Content-Digest values.

Verified in the worktree: `npm run typecheck` exit 0; `npx eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0` exit 0; `npx vitest run tests/simulation-tracking.test.ts tests/simulation-sender.test.ts tests/rtl-logical.test.ts` 20/20 passed. All ten locales carry the six new settings.email keys; no "Aİ"; no ICU-unescaped braces besides {domain}. Nothing under portal/drizzle in the diff; worktree clean.

Not checked: the M365/Workspace step texts against a live tenant (implementer flagged this too); the full vitest suite (orchestrator runs it). Residual risk the owner should know: a scanner that executes JS with an ordinary browser UA still counts — by design, documented.
- [minor] portal/src/server/actions/campaigns.ts:98 `via` is now chosen by the client, not by the route: whoever holds a /t/<token> link can POST the beacon with via "qr" and the recipient's click is emitted as a `qr.scanned` event (webhooks, funnel) instead of `phishing.clicked`. The risk entry and the click itself are identical, so the impact is mislabelled analytics for that one token only. -> Accept as a known limit (one line comment), or have the /q page component call a separate `simulationScanAction` so the route, not the browser, decides the event name.
- [minor] portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts:297 The simulation-domain proof is one-time and sticky and the UI has no way to drop it: once `email.simulationDomain` is set it stays even if the look-alike domain lapses and is registered by a stranger, and simulations keep going out From that domain through the tenant's SMTP (replies and bounces then reach the new registrant). The guide tells admins to clear the address first; nothing enforces it. -> Owner decision (already in left_open). Cheapest hardening if wanted: re-run `domainProofFound` for `simulationDomain` in the existing daily domain re-check and clear `simulationFromAddress` when it has been missing for the same grace period.

Same tenant, same admin, no cross-tenant reach; noting it because the two proofs now mean different things but are indistinguishable in DNS. -> None required; mention in the ADR.

approve
Reviewed the combined diff 1a45970..cd4717e: fea9051 plus the follow-up review-fix commit cd4717e. The worktree contains 1a45970 and nothing under portal/drizzle is committed. The schema change is type-only, inside the JSON settings column, so it needs no migration.

Checks I ran:
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npx eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0`: passed.
- `vitest`: 233 tests passed across simulation-tracking, simulation-sender, drill-service, drill-route, i18n, rtl-logical, settings-schema, settings-rate-limit and tenant-settings.

Acceptance:
(a) Rendering /t or /q only peeks at the token, and `trackingView` no longer imports `recordClick`. A known scanner user agent gets `harvest=false`, so it never sees the sign-in form. `simulationClickAction` validates the token and `via`, refuses scanners, and uses the existing idempotent `recordClick`. The beacon fires on mount for every template, not only harvest ones. /q passes `qr`, which emits `qr.scanned`. The drill still calls `recordClick` directly, and drill-service asserts that clicks and risks are recorded. The tests cover a GET with a browser user agent (nothing recorded), one record per beacon, idempotence, scanner refusal, a bad token and the QR event.
(b) The address can be saved only when its domain equals the stored `simulationDomain`. This is checked before the save and again on the locked row. The proof reuses `domainProofRecord`/`domainProofFound` and the shared domain-check rate limit, and it is audited. Proving a new domain drops an address on the old one. `mail.ts` uses the address only when `kind === 'simulation'`, and retries go through the same `deliverRow`. `withDefaults` keeps the new email keys. Tests cover all of this.
(c) docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md exists and is linked from the portal README, docs/API.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Its claims about the TXT location (`_cyclowareness.` prefix) match `domainProofFound`.
(d) I re-read both digests from registry-1.docker.io: both are `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`, and node `sha256:0820eaa8…` and postgres `sha256:aa6cb33c…` match the pinned values. .github/dependabot.yml has docker and docker-compose entries for /portal, so the README's Dependabot sentence is true.

i18n: all six keys are present in all ten locales, the only ICU placeholder is `{domain}`, and the quoted button and section names match `settings.branding.check` and the domain-proof title in every locale. No physical CSS was added. The new `useState` initialisers derive from props only, so they are hydration-safe.

Not checked: I did not exercise the UI in a browser, and I did not run the full test suite.

A browser without JavaScript (or one where hydration fails) stays on a blank page forever and never sees the lesson. Before this change, such a client saw the login form, and the teach stage behind it, from static HTML. The brief accepts that a JavaScript-less client is not counted, but a blank page with no lesson is a regression the summary does not mention. -> Render a <noscript> fallback inside the beacon stage that shows the teach content (or a link to it), or accept the regression and record it in the ADR trade-off sentence.
- [minor] portal/src/server/services/campaigns.ts:189 The component shows the fake sign-in even when the beacon request fails, so that the lesson is never hidden. recordSubmit, however, now records nothing unless clickedAt is set. A recipient whose beacon failed but who then submits the form is therefore counted as neither a click nor a submit. The tests assert this behaviour on purpose, so it is a known gap rather than a bug. -> No code change needed. Mention it in the ADR trade-off: a failed beacon loses both the click and the submit.
- [nit] portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx:688 saveEmailAction refuses an address on an unproven domain with { ok:false, field:'simulationFromAddress' } and no error or message. The admin gets only the generic field error, not a hint that the domain must be proven first with Check DNS. ## fix
fixed:
Finding 3 (teachable.tsx beacon stage blank without JavaScript): the beacon stage now renders a <noscript> line with the lesson title and a link to /learn/<moduleSlug> (existing site.teach keys, no new strings), so a client without JavaScript or a failed hydration still reaches the teaching content; its click stays uncounted as the brief accepts. File: C:/Users/Safar/Desktop/Cyclowareness- Vol2/.claude/worktrees/wf_42496c94-3d0-4/portal/src/components/site/teachable.tsx
Finding 1 (via chosen by the client): accepted as a known limit with a shortcut comment on simulationClickAction in C:/Users/Safar/Desktop/Cyclowareness- Vol2/.claude/worktrees/wf_42496c94-3d0-4/portal/src/server/actions/campaigns.ts. The suggested separate simulationScanAction was not added: a server action is a public endpoint, so a /t token could be posted to it just as easily; only encoding the channel in the token itself would move the decision to the server, and the impact is one mislabelled event name for that recipient (risk entry and click are identical).
Finding 4 (failed beacon loses click and submit): no code change, as the finding says. ADR trade-off sentence for the orchestrator: 'A click is counted only by the JavaScript beacon; a scanner that fetches the page records nothing, and the price is that a browser whose beacon request fails (or that runs no JavaScript) is counted neither as a click nor, since recordSubmit requires a recorded click, as a submit — it still sees the fake sign-in and then the lesson, or, without JavaScript, a direct link to the lesson.'
rejected:
Finding 2 (simulation-domain proof is sticky and never re-checked): rejected as not cheap and already an owner decision in left_open. The proposed hardening needs two new TenantSettings keys (simulation check timestamp and failing-since), a second concurrency-safe loop in jobs.ts recheckDomains with the same grace-period logic and its own audit entries, plus tests; clearing the address on a single missed lookup without grace would drop the sender on any transient DNS failure. The guide (docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md) already tells admins to clear the simulation sender when a look-alike domain is given up. Open question for the owner stays: should the look-alike domain proof be re-checked daily with the 7-day grace like the organisation domain?
